extracted.intended_audience: The Bulwark editors/writers and readers; center-right journalists and editors deciding story selection
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial guidance for selecting front-page news at The Bulwark from a pro-democracy, center-right perspective — prioritizing threats to democratic continuity and related high-stakes political developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threats to constitutional norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Threats to constitutional norms — especially from the right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that reveal attacks or erosions of constitutional rules and institutions are prioritized; explicit emphasis on threats originating from the political right. Elevate coverage that demonstrates implications for rule of law and separation of powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritarian behavior (patterns over single events)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authoritarian behavior — patterns over single events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer reporting that shows sustained patterns of authoritarian conduct rather than isolated incidents. Emphasize trends, repetition, or systemic behaviors that indicate a shift toward authoritarianism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disinformation tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Disinformation tracking — how false narratives propagate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow and explain the lifecycle and spread of false narratives (who originated them, amplification mechanisms, platforms, political effects). Prioritize stories that clarify mechanisms of disinformation and their democratic impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Republican primary dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Republican primary dynamics — internal GOP battles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover intra-party contests when they reveal fractures, shifts in norms, or movements toward anti-democratic actors or strategies. Prioritize reporting that shows how primary contests affect broader democratic stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Election integrity — both administrative and rhetorical attacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elevate stories about threats to the mechanics of elections (administrative sabotage, legal maneuvers) and rhetorical campaigns undermining trust in results. Tie coverage to real-world risks to free and fair elections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign policy stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign policy stakes — Ukraine, Taiwan, NATO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize international developments with major democratic or geopolitical implications (e.g., Russia/Ukraine, Taiwan/China, NATO unity). Frame foreign-policy coverage in terms of democratic survival and strategic stakes for liberal democracies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial test: survival of liberal democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does this story matter for the survival of liberal democracy?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a core litmus test: stories that materially affect the continued functioning or survival of liberal democratic systems score highest for front-page placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial test: normalization vs. denormalization
rubrics_metrics.description: "Is this normalized behavior that should be denormalized?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether behaviors, rhetoric, or practices are being normalized in ways that threaten democratic norms; prioritize coverage aimed at exposing and reversing normalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial test: mainstream access-driven reticence
rubrics_metrics.description: "Are mainstream outlets pulling punches because of access concerns?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elevate stories when other outlets underreport or soften coverage due to access/insider concerns; look for missed accountability or soft-pedaling by competitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial test: advance understanding vs. trivialize
rubrics_metrics.description: "Does this advance the public's understanding of stakes, or trivialize them?"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer explanatory reporting that deepens public comprehension of the stakes; demote superficial coverage that reduces complex democratic issues to trivia or spectacle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: routine legislative process without democratic stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Day-to-day legislative process without democratic stakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not prioritize mundane legislative coverage unless it connects to threats to democratic norms, accountability, or major public stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: cultural controversies orthogonal to power
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultural controversies orthogonal to power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: De-emphasize culture-war stories that do not illuminate power dynamics or democratic consequences; avoid amplifying sensational but politically irrelevant controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: centrist horse-race coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Centrist horse-race coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid neutral 'horse-race' style political coverage focused on polling and positioning without attention to democratic substance or risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demote: both-sides framing of asymmetric threats
rubrics_metrics.description: Both-sides framing of asymmetric threats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject false equivalence where threats are unequal; do not present asymmetrical, anti-democratic behavior as if it merits balanced framing with defenders of democratic norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: January 6 / accountability stories
rubrics_metrics.description: January 6 / accountability stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize investigative and accountability reporting related to January 6 and its aftermath, including prosecutions, institutional failures, and responsibility of political figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: federal court rulings on executive power
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal court rulings on executive power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight court decisions that affect executive authority, separation of powers, or constitutional limits — especially insofar as they bear on democratic checks and balances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: authoritarianism abroad as warning
rubrics_metrics.description: Authoritarianism abroad as warning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use international examples of democratic erosion as cautionary parallels for domestic politics; contextualize foreign authoritarianism to illuminate risks at home.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: defections/dissent within conservative movement
rubrics_metrics.description: Defections / dissent within conservative movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give prominence to stories about Republicans or conservatives breaking with anti-democratic currents or revealing suppressed truths — these signal internal resistance and are newsworthy for accountability and insight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate: suppressed truths from formerly Republican officials
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppressed truths from formerly Republican officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize revelations or testimony from ex-Republican officials that expose wrongdoing, cover-ups, or threats to democratic norms; these often carry high explanatory and accountability value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overarching lens: stakes-based newsworthiness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bulwark exemplifies "stakes-based" newsworthiness — the rubric is filtered through "what threatens democratic continuity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply an overarching 'stakes' filter to all selection decisions: the primary criterion is whether a story meaningfully illuminates threats to democratic continuity, institutions, or norms. This lens trumps routine political metrics like novelty or partisan balance.
